tool.title: Step 2 · Connect the board
tool.callout: Propeller off: the motor can start by itself.
tool.intro: Plug the board into this computer with a USB data cable and close the Betaflight App. Press Connect and pick the board — its name has “STM32” or “Betaflight” in it.
tool.connect.all: Board not in the list? Show all ports
tool.support.webusb: This browser has no Web Serial, so the tool uses WebUSB instead (Android Chrome with a USB-OTG cable). Some phones keep the port for themselves — then this cannot work here.
tool.support.none: This browser can’t open USB serial ports. Use Chrome, Edge or Opera on Windows, macOS or Linux (or Firefox 151+), or Chrome 148+ on Android with a USB-OTG cable. iPhone and iPad can’t do it: their browsers have no Web Serial or WebUSB.
tool.support.insecure: Open this page over https:// — browsers allow USB access only on secure pages.
tool.mock: Demo mode: a simulated board, nothing real is connected.
tool.status.reconnecting: Board disconnected. Plug it back in — the page reconnects by itself.
tool.status.closed: Disconnected. The board keeps its program and runs it at the next power-on.
tool.status.closedRestart: Disconnected while the board restarted: it runs its program now and the motor may start. A STOP that was waiting is not sent. To stop it, unplug the battery.
tool.status.closedStarting: Disconnected during the countdown: the motor starts soon. To stop it, unplug the battery.
tool.status.closedRunning: Disconnected: the motor keeps running. To stop it, unplug the battery.
tool.status.gaveUp: Stopped waiting for the board (10 min). Plug it in and press Connect — unsaved changes are lost.
tool.back.saved: The board is back and the save is checked:
tool.back.unknown: The board is back. Saved? Unknown — press Save to board again to check.
tool.back.run: The board is back: the program runs from the start.
tool.verdict.other: This doesn’t look like a Shramko Motor Autostart build. Install the firmware first (step 1). Built your own firmware with the module? Check this board.
tool.check.note: Checking reads the settings: the motor stays stopped until you press Run the program.
tool.verdict.notbf: This board runs {variant}, not Betaflight. Install Shramko Motor Autostart first (step 1).
tool.verdict.stock: This board has no autostart yet. Install the firmware first (step 1).
tool.level.old: Firmware 1.0 on this board: no battery protection, run time, gusts or maximum power. Update to 1.1.
tool.live.title: Motor status
tool.live.countdownEsc: Starts in {s} s (the ESC arms first)
tool.live.finishedSub: Press Run the program, or replug the battery, to start again.
tool.live.finishedRc: Turn the RC switch off and on again for a new run.
tool.live.finishedButton: Click the button for a new run.
tool.live.lowSub: Charge the battery, then plug it in again.
tool.live.lowCells: Stopped for low battery at {v} V. The board counts {n}S. If your pack is {g}S ({c} V per cell, charged): set Battery to {g}S in step 3 and save. If it really is {n}S: it is empty, charge it.
tool.live.lowCheck: Stopped for low battery at {v} V. If this is a charged {g}S pack ({c} V per cell), the cell count or stop voltage saved on the board does not fit it: press Change settings and check Battery. Otherwise the pack is empty: charge it.
tool.live.waitBatterySub: Plug in the battery: the motor starts {s} s later.
tool.live.belowVbatMin: The battery shows {v} V, below “Battery counts as plugged in from” ({min} V): nothing starts. Lower it in More settings → Expert.
tool.live.pausedSub: Press Run the program — or switch the board off and on: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery.
tool.live.stoppedSub: Press Run the program — or switch the board off and on: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery.
tool.live.heldSub: Settings, STOP or the Motors tab hold the program: nothing starts until Run the program, or until the board is switched off and on (unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery).
tool.live.heldDoneSub: Held by the computer: press Run the program — or switch the board off and on (unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery). Replugging only the battery does nothing now.
tool.live.heldLowSub: Charge the battery, then switch the board off and on: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery. Replugging only the battery does nothing while the computer holds the program.
tool.live.offSub: The motor never starts by itself (More settings → Start and power).
tool.live.usbHeldSub: A computer is connected (More settings → Outputs and USB).
tool.live.cutUnknown: stop voltage unknown until you open the settings
tool.live.noEsc: No answer from an ESC on any output
tool.live.escWaitTurn: No ESC data yet: over the TX wire the ESC answers only after the motor has turned once.
tool.live.noTelemetry: Not available: connect the ESC’s TX pad to the cable’s yellow wire (feature ESC_SENSOR) — recommended. Bidirectional DShot (dshot_bidir ON, BLHeli_32 32.10 or newer) also works, but a BLHeli_32 that stays on the battery while the board restarts can lock with it: replug the battery after a Save or Run.
tool.live.debugOff: Live status is off on this board.
tool.live.debugStaged: Will be turned on when you press Save to board.
tool.warn.fw10: Firmware 1.0 has no battery protection. Update to 1.1.
tool.warn.noCut: No battery protection: the motor runs until the LiPo is empty.
tool.warn.auto: Cells counted automatically — unreliable with a half-empty pack.
tool.warn.belowStop: {v} V is below the stop voltage {stop} V ({n}S): the motor stops at once and never runs. Check Battery in step 3.
tool.warn.beep: The motor only beeps and does not turn? Unplug the battery and plug it back in: the ESC stayed powered while the board restarted.
tool.hint.beep: Motor only beeps and does not turn after a Save or Run? Unplug the battery and plug it back in (the ESC stayed powered while the board restarted).
tool.warn.implausible: {v} V doesn’t fit {n}S ({c} V per cell). Check Battery in step 3; if the count is right, calibrate the voltage.
tool.warn.implausibleAny: The board’s reading ({v} V) doesn’t fit the battery. Check Battery in step 3; if the cell count is right, calibrate the voltage.
tool.warn.mismatchHigh: The board shows {fc} V, the ESC measures {esc} V ({d} % apart): the board reads high, so the battery stop comes too late.
tool.warn.mismatchLow: The board shows {fc} V, the ESC measures {esc} V ({d} % apart): the board reads low, so the battery stop comes too early (or at once).
tool.stop.sent: Stopped. It stays stopped until you press Run the program — or switch the board off and on: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery.
tool.stop.checking: STOP sent — checking that the motor stopped…
tool.stop.sentNoHold: Stopped. This firmware does not hold the program: plugging the battery in again may start it.
tool.stop.sent10: Stopped. On firmware 1.0 plugging the battery in again starts the program again.
tool.stop.already: The motor is already stopped while the settings are open.
tool.stop.failed: STOP did not reach the board — the motor may still be running. Unplug the battery now.
tool.stop.queued: The board is restarting — the stop is sent the moment it is back.
tool.stop.queuedOff: The board is not connected — the stop is sent the moment it is back. To stop the motor now, unplug the battery.
tool.stop.queuedConnect: The board is still being connected — the stop is sent the moment it answers. To stop the motor now, unplug the battery.
tool.restart.title: Run the motor program now?
tool.restart.body: The board restarts and runs this program:
tool.restart.bodyUnknown: The board restarts and runs the program saved on it. Press Change settings first to see what it does.
tool.restart.unsaved: Your unsaved changes are not used. Save them first.
tool.restart.check: The propeller is off, or nothing and nobody is near it.
tool.restart.done: Board restarted: the program runs from the start.
tool.restart.checking: Board restarted — checking what the program does…
tool.restart.doneOff: Board restarted. Autostart is off: nothing runs.
tool.restart.doneButton: Board restarted: the program starts on a button click.
tool.restart.doneNoBattery: Board restarted: plug in the battery to start the program.
tool.restart.doneIdle: Board restarted. The program did not start: autostart is off, waits for a button, or is held while USB is connected. Press Change settings to see which.
tool.restart.stopped: Board restarted, then stopped with STOP. It stays stopped until you press Run the program — or switch the board off and on: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery.
tool.settings.title: Step 3 · Choose what it does
tool.prog.fresh: Fresh firmware does this (factory settings — this board may differ):
tool.prog.done: If that suits you, you are done: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery.
tool.prog.fw10: Boards flashed with version 1.0 have no battery stop — press Change settings to check.
tool.read.warn: Opening the settings stops the motor until you press Run.
tool.prog.title: What the board will do
tool.prog.titleEdited: What the board will do after saving
tool.prog.start.power: {delay} s after the battery is plugged in
tool.prog.start.powerMin: {delay} s after the battery is plugged in — in fact at least 3 s: the ESC arms first
tool.prog.start.always: {delay} s after the board gets power — it does not wait for a battery
tool.prog.start.alwaysMin: {delay} s after the board gets power (at least 3 s) — it does not wait for a battery
tool.prog.start.off: Never by itself — autostart is off
tool.prog.start.vbatHigh: Never: a {n}S pack never reaches {v} V (Battery counts as plugged in from)
tool.prog.power.steady: Speeds up over {ramp} s to {pct} %, then holds it
tool.prog.power.gusts: Speeds up over {ramp} s to {pct} %, then random gusts of {lo}–{hi} %
tool.prog.power.steadyNow: Goes straight to {pct} % and holds it
tool.prog.power.gustsNow: Goes straight to {pct} %, then random gusts of {lo}–{hi} %
tool.prog.power.gustsOne: Speeds up over {ramp} s to {pct} %, then gusts at {hi} %
tool.prog.power.gustsOneNow: Goes straight to {pct} %, then gusts at {hi} %
tool.prog.power.gustsCap: Speeds up over {ramp} s to {pct} %, then gusts capped at {hi} % by Maximum power
tool.prog.power.gustsCapNow: Goes straight to {pct} %, then gusts capped at {hi} % by Maximum power
tool.prog.power.gustsNone: Speeds up over {ramp} s to {pct} %, then holds it — no gust is above Power (raise Strongest gust)
tool.prog.power.gustsNoneNow: Goes straight to {pct} % and holds it — no gust is above Power (raise Strongest gust)
tool.prog.power.zero: Power is 0 %: the motor does not turn
tool.prog.run.low: Until the battery stays below {v} V ({n} × {cut} V) for {t} s
tool.prog.run.lowAuto: Until the battery stays below {cut} V per cell for {t} s — Betaflight guesses the cell count
tool.prog.run.off: Until the power is off — no battery protection
tool.prog.run.time: {time} after the speed-up; sooner if the battery stays below {v} V
tool.prog.run.timeAuto: {time} after the speed-up; sooner if the battery stays below {cut} V per cell
tool.prog.run.timeOff: {time} after the speed-up — no battery protection
tool.prog.run.fw10: Until the power is off — firmware 1.0 has no battery protection
tool.prog.usb: Nothing spins while a computer is connected
tool.prog.rc: The switch USER{n} on a receiver can run it too — only when the program is idle: after the run time turn it off and on; after a battery stop only a new battery starts it again
tool.note.gustsNone: No gust is above Power ({v} %): every gust runs at Power, i.e. no gusts. Raise Strongest gust.
tool.gusts.tip: About 20 % power between gusts works well.
tool.prot.on: Protected: stops at {v} V ({n} × {c} V), after {t} s
tool.prot.onAuto: Protected roughly: stops at {c} V per cell × the count Betaflight guesses, after {t} s
tool.prot.off: No battery protection: the motor runs until the LiPo is empty
tool.prot.auto: Cells counted automatically — unreliable with a half-empty pack. Pick the number above.
tool.fit.below: {v} V is below the stop voltage {stop} V of {n}S: the motor would stop at once.
tool.legend.battery: stops at {cut} V per cell, after {t} s
tool.legend.expert: battery from {v} V · RC switch: {box} · scale {scale}
tool.legend.expertNoWait: doesn’t wait for a battery · RC switch: {box} · scale {scale}
tool.gusts.off: Turn on Random gusts to set these.
tool.mix.help: Sets only the gusts: 50–90 %, 0.2–0.6 s long, every 1.5–6 s. Power stays as it is.
tool.mix.done: Suggested gust mix set: 50–90 %, 0.2–0.6 s long, every 1.5–6 s.
tool.f.autostart_delay.label: Wait before start
tool.f.autostart_delay.help: Counted from plugging in the battery (or the button click). It never starts sooner than 3 s after the ESC gets power.
tool.f.autostart_throttle.label: Power
tool.f.autostart_throttle.help: How hard the motor blows. With gusts: the level between them. Start low on the bench.
tool.f.autostart_run_time.label: How long
tool.f.autostart_run_time.help: A set time counts after the speed-up. The battery stop works in both cases.
tool.f.autostart_pattern.label: Random gusts
tool.f.autostart_pattern.help: Short strong bursts on top of the steady power, to blow drops off the lens.
tool.f.autostart_cells.label: Battery
tool.f.autostart_cells.help: The cell count of your pack (6 for 6S). The battery stop is cells × the stop voltage per cell.
tool.box.autostart_cells: Count cells automatically (unreliable with a half-empty pack)
tool.cells.autoHelp: Betaflight then guesses the count from the voltage. A half-empty 6S can look like 5S, and the stop comes too late.
tool.f.autostart_mode.label: What starts the motor
tool.f.autostart_mode.help: Battery plugged in is the normal choice. Button click needs a button wired to the board.
tool.f.autostart_ramp.label: Speed-up time
tool.f.autostart_throttle_limit.label: Maximum power
tool.f.autostart_throttle_limit.help: Hard cap for everything the program sends, gusts included. 100 % = no cap.
tool.f.autostart_gust_min.label: Weakest gust
tool.f.autostart_gust_min.help: Lowest gust peak; a peak below Power is raised to Power.
tool.f.autostart_gust_max.label: Strongest gust
tool.f.autostart_gust_max.help: Each gust picks a random peak between the weakest and the strongest.
tool.f.autostart_gust_len_min.label: Shortest gust
tool.f.autostart_gust_len_max.label: Longest gust
tool.f.autostart_gust_pause_min.label: Shortest pause
tool.f.autostart_gust_pause_min.help: Shortest time at the steady power between gusts.
tool.f.autostart_gust_pause_max.label: Longest pause
tool.f.autostart_gust_pause_max.help: Longest time at the steady power between gusts.
tool.f.autostart_cell_cutoff.label: Stop voltage per cell
tool.f.autostart_cell_cutoff.help: Stops the motor when the battery stays below cells × this voltage. 3.30 V suits a LiPo.
tool.box.autostart_cell_cutoff: No battery protection (the LiPo can be ruined)
tool.note.cutLow: The board has {v} V: the firmware uses 2.50 V (the lowest it allows), and saving writes 2.50 V.
tool.f.autostart_cutoff_time.label: Wait before the battery stop
tool.f.autostart_cutoff_time.help: The voltage must stay low this long before the stop (ignores the dip during gusts).
tool.f.autostart_motors.label: Motor outputs
tool.f.autostart_motors.help: Outputs that get the power. 1–4 are the four signal wires of the cable.
tool.note.motor1: The wiring guide connects the ESC to output 1 — keep Motor 1 on.
tool.note.pinio: On this board USER{n} also switches PINIO{n} (another output of the board). Use USER3 or USER4.
tool.f.autostart_usb_inhibit.label: With a computer connected
tool.f.autostart_usb_inhibit.help: Choose whether the motor may spin while USB is plugged in.
tool.f.autostart_vbat_min.label: Battery counts as plugged in from
tool.f.autostart_vbat_min.help: The wait starts when the battery reaches this voltage (vbat_min).
tool.note.vbatHigh: A {n}S pack never reaches {v} V (full: 4.2 V per cell): the motor would never start.
tool.note.vbatLive: The battery now shows {live} V, below {v} V: with this value the motor does not start.
tool.f.autostart_box.label: RC switch
tool.f.autostart_box.help: With a receiver: the AUX mode (USER1–4) that runs the program (autostart_box).
tool.opt.autostart_box.pinio: {user} (also switches PINIO{n} — use USER3 or USER4)
tool.f.vbat_scale.label: Voltage scale (vbat_scale)
tool.f.vbat_scale.help: Board calibration. The helper in Battery sets it from the ESC or a multimeter.
tool.confirm.nocut.title: Turn off battery protection?
tool.confirm.nocut.body: The motor will run until the LiPo is empty, which can ruin the pack.
tool.confirm.auto.title: Count cells automatically?
tool.confirm.auto.body: With a half-empty pack Betaflight can count too few cells, and the battery stop then comes too late.
tool.cal.title: Calibrate the voltage
tool.cal.noReading: Plug in the battery to calibrate: the board shows no voltage.
tool.cal.result: New scale {new} (was {old}). Press Save to board to keep it.
tool.cal.resultEsc: New scale {new} (was {old}) from the ESC’s reading. Press Save to board to keep it.
tool.cal.badInput: Type the voltage your multimeter shows, for example 24.3.
tool.cal.implausible: {v} V doesn’t fit {n}S. 24.4 or 2.44? A {n}S pack reads {lo}–{hi} V. Nothing changed.
tool.cal.clampedRefuse: That would need a scale outside the allowed 10–255: check the reading and the wiring. Nothing changed.
tool.cal.same: The scale already matches ({old}): nothing to change.
tool.cal.escHintOk: The ESC measures {esc} V, the board shows {fc} V ({d} % apart): within 5 %, no calibration needed.
tool.cal.escHintBad: The ESC measures {esc} V, the board shows {fc} V ({d} % apart). More than 5 % apart: calibrate.
tool.cal.escStale: ESC voltage not fresh yet ({v} V may be an old reading): let the motor turn once (Run the program), or use a multimeter.
tool.cal.escOdd: The ESC reports {v} V, which does not fit {n}S: not used. Check the cell count, let the motor turn once, or use a multimeter.
tool.cal.escOddAny: The ESC reports {v} V, which fits no LiPo: not used. Let the motor turn once, or use a multimeter.
tool.cal.escSettling: The battery was just plugged in: the board’s reading settles for a few seconds before it is compared with the ESC.
tool.cal.escClamped: The ESC reports {v} V: that would need a scale outside 10–255, so it is not used. Check the reading and the wiring, or use a multimeter.
tool.cal.escNone: No ESC voltage yet. Without a multimeter: solder the ESC’s TX pad to the cable’s yellow wire (feature ESC_SENSOR) and let the motor turn once; then this box offers the ESC’s reading.
tool.defaults.title: Go back to the defaults?
tool.defaults.body: These change (the voltage calibration is kept):
tool.defaults.note: Defaults are in the form. Press Save to board to apply them.
tool.defaults.none: Everything is already at the defaults.
tool.nochanges.ready: Nothing changed. The board is ready: switch it off and on (unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery), or
tool.save.hint: Saving restarts the board. Keep the propeller off.
tool.undo.done: Changes undone: the form shows the board’s values again.
tool.reload.pending: Save or undo your changes first.
tool.note.swapped: Swapped so the smaller value comes first.
tool.note.mask: At least one output must stay on.
tool.note.runMin: At least 1 s: set to 1 s.
tool.step.reconnect: Waiting for the board to come back…
tool.step.verify: Reading back to check every value…
tool.saved.one: Saved and checked on the board: {n} value.
tool.saved.other: Saved and checked on the board: {n} values.
tool.saved.after: The motor stays stopped until you press Run now — or switch the board off and on: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery.
tool.saved.swapped: Swapped so the smaller value comes first: {list}.
tool.err.no-api: This browser can’t open USB serial ports. Use Chrome, Edge or Opera on a computer (or Firefox 151+), or Chrome 148+ on Android with a USB-OTG cable.
tool.err.insecure: Open this page over https:// — browsers allow USB access only on secure pages.
tool.err.cancelled: No port selected. Press Connect again and pick the board’s port.
tool.err.permission: The browser or the system refused access to the port. Allow USB access and try again.
tool.err.busy: The port is busy. Close the Betaflight App (and any other program using the board), then press Connect again.
tool.err.not-open: The board is not connected. Press Connect.
tool.err.lost: The board disconnected. Plug it back in; the page reconnects by itself.
tool.err.lost-connect: The board disconnected while connecting. Plug it in and press Connect.
tool.err.timeout: The board stopped answering. Unplug it, plug it back in and press Connect.
tool.err.reconnect-timeout: The board did not come back after restarting. Unplug the USB cable and plug it back in — the page keeps waiting and reconnects by itself.
tool.err.no-answer: This port doesn’t answer like a Betaflight flight controller. Pick the board’s port (often “STM32 Virtual ComPort”), or close the Betaflight App.
tool.err.msp-error: The board refused a request. Check that it runs Betaflight 2025.12.
tool.err.cli: The board’s command line did not answer. Unplug and replug the board, then try again.
tool.err.cli-invalid-value: The board refused {name} = {value}. Nothing was saved.
tool.err.cli-invalid-name: This firmware has no setting {name}. Nothing was saved — update the firmware.
tool.err.verify: Saved, but the board kept different values: {list}. Try again; if it repeats, tell us with the Feedback button.
tool.err.not-saved: The board disconnected before it could save. Nothing was saved — press Save to board again.
tool.err.not-ours: The autostart module is not on this board.
tool.err.busy-op: Wait for the current step to finish.
tool.err.internal: Something went wrong on our side ({msg}). Please tell us with the Feedback button.
tool.err.not-usb: That port is a Bluetooth device (headphones, a phone link), not the board. Press Connect and pick the board — its name has “STM32” or “Betaflight” in it.
tool.restart.doneNoLive: Board restarted. Without live status the page cannot see what the program does now: press Change settings to see the program saved on the board.
